newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open mixed before BOP data.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open mixed before BOP data.

text.p: Australian shares opened mixed to slightly firmer on Wednesday ahead of the release of September current account data and after a rally on Wall Street.
At 10.20 a.m. (2320 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was one point higher at 2,324.0. Holding back the market early was a fall in the price of BHP whose shares were ex-dividend 25 cents.
"The market has still opened firmer despite the fact that BHP has gone ex-dividend and this augurs well for the market," a dealer from a Sydney-based brokerage said.

The dealer said the market had discounted softer base metal prices and was focusing on the knowledge that metal inventories had continued to fall. "The longer term outlook for base metals is still more positive than it had been for some time," he said.
The industrial sector started firmer with the bank and insurance sectors spurred by a local bond market rally after U.S. Treasuries posted strong rises on Tuesday.
The most active stocks early were major banks Westpac and ANZ, both of which opened slightly firmer.
